definition_zh: 致力于；献身；专用于
definition_en: to give all or most of your time and energy to something
core_image: 台灯下摊开的书，旁边放着一杯早已凉透的茶
scene: 深夜的书房只剩一盏台灯，桌上的茶早已凉透。 She devoted every evening to studying old maps.
sceneCN: 这里 devote 指「致力于」（第 1 个义项：把时间和精力全给某件事）；句意是她每个晚上都用来研究古地图。

derivatives.zh: 献身；挚爱；虔诚
忠诚的；挚爱的
忠实地；专心地
爱好者；信徒

senses.title: Give time and energy
senses.definition: to give most of your time and energy to an activity
senses.definitionCN: 把大部分时间和精力投入某项活动
senses.example: She devoted every evening to studying old maps.
senses.exampleCN: 她每个晚上都用来研究古地图。
senses.why: Time is the one thing you can only spend once, so giving it is a real gift.
senses.whyCN: 时间只能花一次，所以把它给出去才是真的给。

senses.title: Give yourself fully
senses.definition: to give yourself completely to a person, cause or duty
senses.definitionCN: 把自己完全交给某个人、某项事业或某种责任
senses.example: He devoted his life to caring for the poor.
senses.exampleCN: 他把一生献给了照顾穷人。
senses.why: A life laid down on one purpose is the oldest kind of offering.
senses.whyCN: 把一生铺在一个目标上，是最古老的一种奉献。

senses.title: Set aside for one purpose
senses.definition: to give a place, page or period completely to one subject
senses.definitionCN: 把某处空间、某页或某段时间完全留给一个主题
senses.example: The last chapter is devoted to local birds.
senses.exampleCN: 最后一章专门讲本地的鸟。
senses.why: A marked space is a promise that this subject will be met.
senses.whyCN: 划出来的一块地方，是「一定会谈这个」的承诺。

intro.en: Devote comes from Latin devovere, to vow away, built from de- and vovere, to vow, and it entered English through French.
intro.cn: devote 来自拉丁语 devovere（许愿献出），由 de- 与 vovere（发誓）构成，经法语进入英语。

items.en: Vovere meant to make a solemn vow.
items.cn: vovere 指郑重地立誓。

items.en: Devovere meant to vow something away, often to the gods.
items.cn: devovere 指把某物许愿献出去，常是献给神。

items.en: Devotio named the act of dedication, and also a curse.
items.cn: devotio 指奉献这一行为，也曾带诅咒之意。

items.en: English devote came to mean giving oneself to a worthy purpose.
items.cn: 英语 devote 渐渐指把自己交给一个值得的目标。

items.en: It now covers time, attention, whole lives and even single chapters.
items.cn: 如今它覆盖时间、注意力、一生，甚至单独的一章。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the devot stem, while the meaning group moves from pledging to committing and consecrating.
note.cn: 形近组共用 devot 这个词干，近义组则从许诺走到投入与奉献。

normalIntro.en: These hooks begin with a lamp over one open book and end with a chapter given to a single subject.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从照着一本摊开的书的台灯开始，落到专门留给一个主题的一章。

normal.en: To devote is to make a vow and then pay it in hours.
normal.cn: devote 就是先立一个誓，再用小时去还。

normal.en: The tea goes cold because the book is warmer.
normal.cn: 茶凉了，是因为那本书更热。

normal.en: A whole life can be given to one small duty.
normal.cn: 整条命也能交给一件小小的责任。

normal.en: A chapter devoted to birds is a room built for them.
normal.cn: 专门讲鸟的一章，就是为它们盖的一间房。

normal.en: Attention is the modern form of the old offering.
normal.cn: 注意力，就是古老奉献的现代样式。

abstract.en: Picture an empty chair pulled close to a desk.

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 devote 记成「地沃特」：de 是向下，vot 是发誓，低头立誓把时间交出去，就是致力于与献身。

root: 来自拉丁语 devovere，由 de-（向下、彻底）与 vovere（立誓）组成，经法语进入英语。本义是许愿献出，常指献给神明，十六世纪起转为把自己交给某个目标，再引申为把时间、空间或篇幅专门留给某事物。

sensesIntro.en: From a vow paid in hours, to a whole life handed over, to one chapter set aside for one subject.
sensesIntro.cn: 从用小时去还的誓，到交出整条命，再到为一件事留出的一章。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a lamp burning late over a single open book.
core.cn: 核心意象：一盏灯为一本摊开的书亮到很晚。

branches.en: The first sense is the hours handed over one by one.
branches.cn: 第一个义项是一个小时一个小时交出去。

branches.en: The second sense is the whole of a life handed over at once.
branches.cn: 第二个义项是把整条命一次交出去。

branches.en: The third sense is a space marked off for one subject.
branches.cn: 第三个义项是为一个主题划出来的一块地方。

branches.en: Hours and a lifetime differ only in how many payments are made.
branches.cn: 小时与一生，只差在付了多少次。

branches.en: A given life and a given page both say: this matters most.
branches.cn: 交出的一生与交出的一页都在说：这个最重要。

intro.en: Devote has a family built on vows, loyalty and the giving of oneself.
intro.cn: devote 有一族词，建在誓言、忠诚与交出自己之上。

latinIntro.en: The base is Latin vovere, to vow, and de- adds the sense of giving away completely.
latinIntro.cn: 词基是拉丁语 vovere（立誓），前缀 de- 添上完全交出的意思。

items.exampleCN: 他们投入很多小时练习。

items.example: He is a devotee of old films.
He devotes Sundays to his family.
Devoting a year to travel changed her.
items.exampleCN: 用一年去旅行改变了她。

definition_zh: 迫使；使不得不；施恩于；帮……的忙；应允；效劳；感激；感谢
definition_en: to force someone to do something by law, duty or circumstance; also to do someone a favour, to comply with a request, and to be grateful for a kindness
core_image: 一根看不见的绳子把人牵向唯一的选择，绳子的另一头却系着一份人情
scene: 暴雨冲垮了唯一的渡口，赶路的人被困在河岸上，前后都没有别的路可走。 The flooded river obliged the travellers to wait for a boat.
sceneCN: 这里是「迫使、使不得不」（第 1 个义项：因法律、职责或形势而不得不做）；句意为暴涨的河水逼得行人只能等船。可辨物件：浑黄的河水、岸边的行囊、断掉的木桥。

pos.zh: 迫使；使负有义务；施恩于

collocations.zh: 非常感谢（旧式客气说法）

derivatives.zh: 由 oblige 加名词后缀 -ation 构成，义为「义务；责任；债务」
由 oblige 的词干加 -atory 构成，义为「必须的；强制的」
由 oblige 加 -ing 构成，义为「乐于助人的；殷勤的」
由 obliging 加 -ly 构成，义为「殷勤地；乐意地」

senses.title: To force someone by law, duty or circumstances
senses.definition: to make someone do something because of a law, a duty or the pressure of events
senses.definitionCN: 因法律、职责或形势的压力而使人不得不做某事
senses.example: Heavy snow obliged the climbers to turn back.
senses.exampleCN: 大雪迫使登山者折返。
senses.why: The Latin verb obligare meant to bind up, and a law or a storm acts like a rope that leaves a person only one course of action.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 obligare 本义是「捆住」，法律、职责或一场暴风雪都像绳子一样把人拴在唯一的选择上，于是有了「迫使」。

senses.title: To do someone a service or favour
senses.definition: to help someone by doing what they have asked, as a favour
senses.definitionCN: 按对方的请求出力，作为一种好意
senses.example: Our host obliged us with a lift to the station.
senses.exampleCN: 主人开车送我们去了车站。
senses.why: A kindness puts the receiver in the giver's debt, so the verb for binding also came to mean laying a soft obligation of gratitude on someone.
senses.whyCN: 一份好意让受助者欠下人情，于是那个表示「捆住」的动词，转而指用善意把对方轻轻系在自己这一边。

senses.title: To comply with a request; willing to help
senses.definition: to do what someone has asked, often willingly and without any pressure
senses.definitionCN: 按别人的请求去做，往往是自愿的、没有压力的
senses.example: The shop assistant obliged when I asked for another size.
senses.exampleCN: 我请店员换一个尺码，她很爽快地答应了。
senses.why: Here the bond is chosen rather than imposed: the helper ties his own action to another person's request, and the adjective obliging names that temperament.
senses.whyCN: 这里的「捆」不是被强加的，而是自己选的：帮忙的人把自己的行动系在别人的请求上，形容词 obliging 正形容这种性情。

senses.title: To be grateful for a favour received
senses.definition: used in the phrase be obliged to someone, meaning to be thankful for a kindness
senses.definitionCN: 用于 be obliged to 这一说法，表示因受恩惠而心存感谢
senses.example: I am much obliged to you for your help.
senses.exampleCN: 承蒙相助，我不胜感激。
senses.why: A favour leaves the receiver bound to the giver, and English turned that bond into a polite formula of thanks.
senses.whyCN: 受了恩惠的人觉得自己欠着对方，英语就把这条人情之绳固化成客气的致谢说法，be obliged to 由此表示感激。

intro.en: Oblige comes from a Latin verb that literally means to bind, and that rope shows up in every one of its senses.
intro.cn: oblige 来自一个字面意思为「捆绑」的拉丁动词，而这条绳子出现在它的每一个义项里。

items.en: Ligare meant to tie or bind, and it stands behind ligament and the whole family of words about obligation.
items.cn: ligare 意为捆绑、系住，是 ligament 以及整个「义务」词族的共同词根。

items.en: The prefix ob- joined ligare to make obligare, to bind up or fasten, and then to bind a person by promise or duty.
items.cn: 前缀 ob- 与 ligare 合成 obligare，本义是把东西捆好、扎紧，再引申为用承诺或职责把人约束住。

items.en: Old French obliger kept both jobs: to bind someone by a pledge and, by extension, to lay a kindness on someone.
items.cn: 古法语 obliger 同时保留两种用法：用誓言约束某人，以及引申为把一份好意施加于某人。

items.en: English borrowed the verb for moral and legal binding, then for the favour that puts another in one's debt.
items.cn: 英语借入这个动词，先指道德与法律上的约束，再指那种让受助者欠下人情的帮忙。

items.en: Modern English keeps the force sense as the main one, while the polite phrase much obliged survives as a formal thank-you.
items.cn: 现代英语以「迫使」为主要义项，而客气话 much obliged 作为正式的致谢一直沿用至今。

note.en: The look-alike group collects relatives built on the Latin root for binding; the near-meaning group collects words for compulsion and for gratitude.
note.cn: 形近组收建立在「捆绑」这一拉丁词根上的同族词，近义组收表示强制与感激的词。

entries.definitionCN: 一个人有义务去做的事。

entries.definition: Willing to help and quick to do favours.

entries.definition: To make someone do something they do not want to do.

normalIntro.en: The word is a rope in disguise: ligare means to bind, and each sense shows a different kind of tie.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词其实是一条化装的绳子：ligare 意为捆绑，每个义项都呈现一种不同的系法。

normal.en: The core of obligare is ligare, to bind, so oblige starts as the act of tying a person to a duty.
normal.cn: obligare 的核心是 ligare（捆绑），所以 oblige 一开始就是把一个人拴在责任上的动作。

normal.en: Obligation adds -ation to the verb and names the rope itself: the duty that holds a person.
normal.cn: obligation 在动词后加 -ation，指的是绳子本身，也就是约束人的那份义务。

normal.en: Obliging drops the force and keeps only the willingness, which is why it means helpful.
normal.cn: obliging 去掉了强制，只留下自愿，因此表示「乐于助人的」。

normal.en: Much obliged is a polite way of saying that kindness has bound you to the other person.
normal.cn: much obliged 是一种客气说法，意思是对方的善意把你系住了。

normal.en: Noblesse oblige joins the word with nobility: high rank brings duties rather than privileges.
normal.cn: noblesse oblige 把这个词与贵族相连：高地位带来的是责任，而不是特权。

abstract.en: Picture one rope that is now a law, now a storm, now a favour.
abstract.cn: 想象同一根绳子，一会儿是法律，一会儿是暴风雪，一会儿是一份好意。

abstract.en: The same word can push and can thank, because both are ways of being tied to another person.
abstract.cn: 同一个词既能推人向前，也能道谢，因为两者都是被系在别人身上的方式。

abstract.en: A favour is a soft rope: nobody forces you, yet you still feel the pull.
abstract.cn: 好意是一根柔软的绳子：没人强迫你，你仍然感到那股拉力。

examples.en: Heavy snow obliged the climbers to turn back.
examples.cn: 大雪迫使登山者折返。

examples.en: Our host obliged us with a lift to the station.
examples.cn: 主人开车送我们去了车站。

examples.en: I am much obliged to you for your help.
examples.cn: 承蒙相助，我不胜感激。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「哦不来这」——形势逼着人，哦，不来这儿也不行；记住 oblige 是迫使。

root: 拉丁语 ob-（朝向、对着）+ ligare（捆绑）→ obligare（捆住、使负有义务）→ 古法语 obliger → 英语 oblige；同族词多与约束、义务有关。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a bond; the senses divide into being bound by law or circumstance, binding another by kindness, willingly accepting a request, and thanking the one who bound you.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「捆绑」；义项分成被法律或形势拴住、用善意系住别人、自愿应承请求，以及向系住自己的人道谢。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an invisible rope pulling a person toward the only choice left, while a favour hangs from the other end.
core.cn: 核心意象：一根看不见的绳子把人牵向唯一的选择，绳子的另一端还系着一份人情。

branches.cn: 店员找出另一个尺码

branches.en: a helper tying himself to another's request
branches.cn: 帮忙的人自愿应承别人的请求

branches.en: a letter ending with a warm word of thanks
branches.cn: 信末一句温暖的致谢

intro.en: The word is held together by a Latin verb for binding, the prefix that points it at a person, a French verb, and two English suffixes that build a quality and a duty.
intro.cn: 这个词由表示捆绑的拉丁动词、把人指向对象的前缀、一个法语动词，以及两个分别造出「性质」与「义务」的英语后缀共同支撑。

latinIntro.en: Latin ligare supplies the rope, and obligare, obligatio and the related noun obligator carry it into English.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 ligare 提供了那根绳子，obligare、obligatio 以及相关的 obligator 把它带进英语。

definition_zh: 减弱；削弱；使变弱；变弱
definition_en: to make someone or something less strong, or to become less strong
core_image: 一根木梁上一道裂缝慢慢变宽，撑不住屋顶了
scene: 洪水退去后，桥墩上留下一道细缝，几个月后那道缝已经宽得能插进手指。 Flood water had weakened the bridge pier until the crack widened.
sceneCN: 这里 weaken 是「削弱」（第 1 个义项：使某物力量变小）；句意为洪水把桥墩削弱了，裂缝越变越宽。那道慢慢变宽、撑不住屋顶的裂缝就是这个词的印象。

derivatives.zh: 弱的；虚弱的
虚弱；弱点
削弱者；削弱物
减弱；削弱
未被削弱的

senses.title: To make something less strong
senses.definition: to reduce the strength, force or solidity of something
senses.definitionCN: 降低某物的力量、强度或坚固程度
senses.example: Repeated flooding weakened the bridge pier.
senses.exampleCN: 反复的洪水削弱了桥墩。
senses.why: The verb simply turns the adjective into an action: to give weakness to something.
senses.whyCN: 这个动词把形容词变成动作：把弱加给某物。

senses.title: To become less strong
senses.definition: to lose strength or force without an outside agent
senses.definitionCN: 在没有外力作用下失去力量或强度
senses.example: His voice weakened as the evening went on.
senses.exampleCN: 夜渐深，他的声音越来越弱。
senses.why: English -en verbs work both ways, so weaken can act alone as well as on an object.
senses.whyCN: 英语的 -en 动词可及物也可不及物，故 weaken 既能带宾语也能单独使用。

senses.title: To reduce power or influence
senses.definition: to make a person, group or institution less powerful or effective
senses.definitionCN: 使人、团体或机构的力量或效能变小
senses.example: The scandal weakened the minister’s position in the party.
senses.exampleCN: 这桩丑闻削弱了这位部长在党内的地位。
senses.why: Power and influence are kinds of strength, so a loss of them is weakening too.
senses.whyCN: 权力与影响力也是某种力量，失去它们同样是「被削弱」。

senses.title: To make an argument or case less convincing
senses.definition: to make a claim, excuse or argument less persuasive
senses.definitionCN: 使主张、借口或论据不那么有说服力
senses.example: One false date weakens the whole report.
senses.exampleCN: 一个错误的日期就能让整份报告站不住脚。
senses.why: Influence and credibility are kinds of strength, so loss of them is also weakening.
senses.whyCN: 影响力与可信度都是某种力量，失去它们同样是「变弱」。

senses.title: To become less intense or less firm
senses.definition: of a feeling or determination, to become less firm
senses.definitionCN: 指情绪或决心变得不那么坚定
senses.example: She refused at first, but her resolve weakened at the last minute.
senses.exampleCN: 她起初拒绝了，但最后一刻决心动摇了。
senses.why: Determination is felt as a force that holds firm, and it thins the way a rope does.
senses.whyCN: 决心被感受为一股撑住不倒的力量，会像绳子那样变松变细。

intro.en: Weaken is an English verb made from weak plus the suffix -en, the same pattern as deepen and widen.
intro.cn: weaken 是由 weak 加后缀 -en 构成的英语动词，与 deepen、widen 属于同一模式。

items.en: The adjective weak came into English from veikr, a Norse word for giving way.
items.cn: 形容词 weak 从意为退让的诺斯词 veikr 进入英语。

items.en: Once weak was in everyday use, speakers began to make a verb of it with the native -en ending.
items.cn: weak 进入日常用法后，人们开始用本土词尾 -en 把它变成动词。

items.en: Weaken appeared beside similar pairs such as hard and harden, wide and widen.
items.cn: weaken 与 hard、harden，wide、widen 这类成对形式并列出现。

items.en: The verb is used of bodies, structures, currencies and arguments alike.
items.cn: 这个动词既用于身体、结构，也用于货币与论据。

items.en: The participle weakened is common in the passive, as in weakened by years of neglect.
items.cn: 过去分词 weakened 在被动语态中很常见，如「因长年失修而受损」。

note.en: The first group is the weak family itself, the second the verbs that do similar work.
note.cn: 第一组是 weak 词族本身，第二组是做类似工作的动词。

Something that makes another thing weaker.

To damage a faculty or function.
To make or become smaller.
To weaken something by adding water or another element.

normalIntro.en: Weaken is the simplest way English turns an adjective into a verb: add -en and the quality becomes a change.
normalIntro.cn: weaken 是英语把形容词变动词的最简单办法：加 -en，性质就变成变化。

normal.en: Weak is what something is; weaken is what happens to it.
normal.cn: weak 是事物是什么样，weaken 是它遭遇了什么。

normal.en: Deepen, widen, harden, weaken all use the same -en.
normal.cn: deepen、widen、harden、weaken 都用同一个 -en。

normal.en: You can weaken a bridge, a case or a currency.
normal.cn: 桥、论据、货币都可以被削弱。

normal.en: The passive weakened by illness is very common.
normal.cn: 被动式 weakened by illness 很常见。

normal.en: Weakening is also the noun, as in a weakening of demand.
normal.cn: weakening 也是名词，如需求减弱。

abstract.en: Watch a hairline crack open wider each winter.
abstract.cn: 想一道细缝在每个冬天都裂得更宽。

abstract.en: Feel a grip loosen one finger at a time.
abstract.cn: 感受一次握手一根手指一根手指地松开。

abstract.en: Hear a drumbeat that slowly loses its force.
abstract.cn: 听鼓点一点点失去力道。

examples.en: Years of rain have weakened the stone wall.
examples.cn: 多年的雨水侵蚀使这堵石墙变弱了。

examples.en: The illness left him weakened for a whole month.
examples.cn: 这场病让他虚弱了整整一个月。

examples.en: Such excuses only weaken your case.
examples.cn: 这样的借口只会让你的论点站不住脚。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「威肯」——威肯工程师发现桥墩有缝，赶紧报告：这些裂缝正在削弱桥体。

root: 古诺斯语 veikr（易弯、退让）→ weak；加英语后缀 -en 构成动词 weaken，与 deepen、widen 同类。

sensesIntro.en: The verb starts with a structure losing solidity, then widens to power, arguments and finally to determination.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个动词从结构失去坚固出发，再扩展到权力、论据，最后是决心。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a crack in a beam opening wider.
core.cn: 核心意象：梁上的一道裂缝越变越宽。

branches.en: The structural branch: flood water and a bridge pier.
branches.cn: 结构分支：洪水与桥墩。

branches.en: The self-acting branch: a voice fading at night.
branches.cn: 自变分支：夜里逐渐弱下去的声音。

branches.en: The power branch: a minister’s position damaged.
branches.cn: 权力分支：受损的部长地位。

branches.en: The argument branch: one wrong date spoils a report.
branches.cn: 论据分支：一个错误日期毁掉报告。

branches.en: The will branch: resolve that gives way late.
branches.cn: 意志分支：最后一刻动摇的决心。

intro.en: Weaken is a native derivation: an adjective from Old Norse plus the English suffix -en.
intro.cn: weaken 是本土派生：一个来自古诺斯语的形容词加上英语后缀 -en。

latinIntro.en: Neither part is Latin, so the Latin table only records the Norse adjective behind weak.
latinIntro.cn: 两部分都不来自拉丁语，故拉丁表只记 weak 背后的诺斯形容词。

items.example: It turns the adjective into a verb.

definition_zh: 口头的；口部的；口服的；口试
definition_en: spoken rather than written, or relating to the mouth; as a noun, an examination in which answers are spoken
core_image: 两个人面对面坐着，声音从嘴里出来，桌上没有纸笔
scene: 面试的小房间里，考官只开口提问，桌上没有纸笔，考生只能凭说话作答。 The final exam includes an oral test that lasts ten minutes.
sceneCN: 这里 oral 是「口试」（第 4 个义项：以口头问答进行的考试）；句意为期末考试含一场十分钟的口试，画面是没有纸笔的小房间与面对面的两个人。

derivatives.zh: 由 oral 加副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「口头地；经口地」
由 oral 加名词后缀 -ity 构成，义为「口头性；口述传统」
由 oral 加表示「主义、方法」的后缀 -ism 构成，义为「口语法；口语教学法」

senses.title: Spoken rather than written
senses.definition: expressed by speaking rather than by writing
senses.definitionCN: 通过说话表达，而非通过书写
senses.example: The company gave only an oral warning, with nothing in writing.
senses.exampleCN: 公司只作了口头警告，没有留下任何书面内容。
senses.why: Latin os, genitive oris, meant mouth, so what is oral comes out of the mouth rather than off the page.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 os（属格 oris）指「嘴」，所以 oral 的事物是从嘴里出来的，而不是从纸面来的；「口头」这一层直接由「嘴」引出。

senses.title: Relating to the mouth
senses.definition: relating to the mouth as a part of the body or to care of it
senses.definitionCN: 与作为身体部位的嘴有关，或与口腔护理有关
senses.example: Good oral hygiene protects the teeth and gums.
senses.exampleCN: 良好的口腔卫生保护牙齿与牙龈。
senses.why: The same body part that produces speech also needs care, so the word keeps the plain anatomical sense beside the speaking one.
senses.whyCN: 同一个身体部位既发出话语，也需要被照料，所以这个词在「说话」之外保留了朴素的解剖义；这是词根本义的直接延伸。

senses.title: Taken by mouth, of medicine
senses.definition: of a medicine, taken through the mouth rather than injected or applied to the skin
senses.definitionCN: 指药物经口服用，而不是注射或涂在皮肤上
senses.example: The doctor changed her to an oral antibiotic.
senses.exampleCN: 医生给她换成了口服抗生素。
senses.why: Because the mouth is the entrance to the body, a remedy swallowed through it is named with the same adjective.
senses.whyCN: 嘴是身体的一个入口，所以经口吞下的药也用同一个形容词来命名；「口部」的空间意义由此转成了用药途径。

senses.title: A spoken examination
senses.definition: an examination in which a candidate answers questions by speaking rather than by writing
senses.definitionCN: 考生以口头回答、而非笔试作答的考试
senses.example: She passed the oral and moved on to the written part.
senses.exampleCN: 她通过了口试，接着进入笔试部分。
senses.why: When the adjective names the spoken form, it can stand alone as a noun for the spoken test itself.
senses.whyCN: 当形容词指明「口头的形式」，它就能单独作名词，指口头形式的考试本身；这是省略所修饰名词之后的形容词名词化。

intro.en: Oral comes from the Latin word for mouth and its adjective oralis; the sense of speech grew out of that plain bodily meaning.
intro.cn: oral 出自拉丁语中表示「嘴」的词及其形容词 oralis；「口头」的意思是从这个朴素的身体义长出来的。

items.en: The Latin noun os meant mouth, and its genitive stem or- is the part that reached later words.
items.cn: 拉丁语名词 os 意为「嘴」，其属格词干 or- 进入了后来的词。

items.en: Oralis was formed on that stem to mean of the mouth, a plain adjective of the body.
items.cn: oralis 在这一词干上构成，意为「口的」，本是一个朴素的身体形容词。

items.en: French oral carried both the anatomical sense and the sense of what is spoken rather than written.
items.cn: 法语 oral 兼有解剖义与「说而非写」的意思。

items.en: English borrowed oral for things of the mouth, and the spoken sense grew beside it in learned and legal use.
items.cn: 英语借入 oral 指与嘴有关的事物，「口头的」这层意思在学术与法律用法中随之生长。

items.en: Modern English uses oral for speech, for mouth care, for medicine taken by mouth, and for the spoken test.
items.cn: 现代英语用 oral 指口头表达、口腔护理、口服药物，以及口头进行的考试。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers forms on the Latin mouth-stem and two words that only resemble them in spelling; the near-meaning group gathers words for speech and for a spoken test.
note.cn: 形近组收建立在拉丁语「嘴」词干上的形式，以及两个只是拼写相近的词；近义组收表示言语与口头考试的词。

entries.definition: In speech, or through the mouth.
An opening or hole, especially one in the body, built from the Latin mouth-word and the verb to make.
entries.definitionCN: 开口；孔洞，尤指身体上的孔口，由拉丁语「嘴」与「做」的动词构成。

entries.definition: A skilled public speaker; the spelling resembles oral, but the word comes from Latin orare, to speak, a different root.
entries.definitionCN: 擅长公开演说的人；拼写与 oral 相近，但词源是拉丁语 orare（说话），只是拼写相近，词根不同。

entries.definition: A formal speech given on an important occasion; it shares the speaking root of orator, not the mouth root of oral.
entries.definitionCN: 在重要场合发表的正式演说；它与 orator 同出「说话」词根，而非 oral 的「嘴」词根。

entries.definition: Expressed in speech rather than in writing.
entries.definitionCN: 以说话而非书写表达的。

entries.definition: Relating to words, especially to speech rather than writing.
entries.definitionCN: 与词语有关的，尤指口头而非书面的。

entries.definition: An oral examination, especially one held in a university.
entries.definitionCN: 口试，尤指大学里的口头答辩。

normalIntro.en: The word grows straight out of the Latin mouth, and its family keeps returning to the body, to speech and to the test taken by voice.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词直接从拉丁语「嘴」长出来，同族用法反复回到身体、言语与以声音作答的考试。

normal.en: Os and its genitive oris mean mouth, and oralis adds -alis, so oral is an adjective laid directly on the body part.
normal.cn: os 及其属格 oris 意为「嘴」，oralis 再加 -alis，所以 oral 是直接加在身体部位上的形容词。

normal.en: The same mouth-root gives orifice, an opening, because a mouth is a hole in the body.
normal.cn: 同一「嘴」词根还给出 orifice（开口），因为嘴就是身体上的一个孔。

normal.en: Orator looks close but comes from orare, to speak, so the likeness is spelling rather than a shared root.
normal.cn: orator 看起来相近，却出自 orare（说话），所以相似处是拼写，而不是同一词根。

normal.en: Oral history and oral tradition keep the spoken sense, where words live in voices rather than on paper.
normal.cn: oral history 与 oral tradition 保留口头义，在那里话语活在声音里，而不在纸上。

normal.en: In medicine oral marks the route through the mouth, and in school it marks the spoken test, both still anchored to the body.
normal.cn: 医学里 oral 标出经口途径，学校里 oral 标出用口作答的考试，两处都仍锚定在身体上。

abstract.en: A small room with two chairs, no paper and no pens, is the word oral reduced to its scene.
abstract.cn: 一间只摆两把椅子的小屋，没有纸也没有笔，就是把 oral 还原成场景。

abstract.en: A spoon of syrup going in through the mouth shows the body used as a doorway, which is the medical sense of the word.
abstract.cn: 一勺糖浆从嘴里送进去，显示身体被当作一道门，这就是这个词的医学义。

abstract.en: A student answers aloud while an examiner listens, and the spoken answer becomes the exam itself.
abstract.cn: 学生出声作答、考官在旁倾听，口头的回答于是变成了考试本身。

examples.en: The final exam includes an oral test that lasts ten minutes.
examples.cn: 期末考试含一场十分钟的口试。

examples.en: The company gave only an oral warning, with nothing in writing.
examples.cn: 公司只作了口头警告，没有留下任何书面内容。

examples.en: Good oral hygiene protects the teeth and gums.
examples.cn: 良好的口腔卫生保护牙齿与牙龈。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「噢，若」——只在嘴上说、不动笔；oral 意为口头的。

root: 拉丁语 os（属格 oris，嘴）→ 晚期拉丁 oralis（口的）→ 法语 oral → 英语 oral；由「嘴」引申为「口头的」，再作名词指口试。

sensesIntro.en: The core is the mouth; the senses spread from what the mouth produces in speech, to care of the mouth, to medicine taken through it, to the spoken test.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「嘴」；义项从嘴在言语中产生的东西，扩展到口腔的照料、经口服下的药，再到以口作答的考试。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two people facing each other, words leaving the mouth, no paper on the table.
core.cn: 核心意象：两个人面对面，话从嘴里出来，桌上没有纸笔。

branches.en: an interview room with no paper and no pens
branches.cn: 没有纸笔的面试小房间

branches.en: a doctor looking into a patient's mouth
branches.cn: 医生查看病人的口腔

branches.en: a spoon of syrup taken through the mouth
branches.cn: 一勺经口服下的糖浆

branches.en: a student answering aloud while an examiner listens
branches.cn: 学生出声作答，考官倾听

branches.en: the same spoken act, once as a warning and once as a test
branches.cn: 同一种口头行为，一次是警告，一次是考试

intro.en: The word rests on the Latin noun for mouth, its genitive stem, a late adjective, and two English endings that make the adverb and the noun-like form.
intro.cn: 这个词依托拉丁语中表示「嘴」的名词、它的属格词干、一个晚期形容词，以及两个构成副词与类名词形式的英语词尾。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

items.meaning: genitive of os, of the mouth

definition_zh: 充足的；丰富的；丰产的；大量的
definition_en: existing in amounts that are enough or more than enough, especially of a supply, a harvest or repeated instances
core_image: 秋收后的谷仓，麻袋一直码到房梁，伸手就还能再拖一袋
scene: 秋收过后的谷仓里，麻袋一直码到房梁，农户随手还能再拖下一袋。 A plentiful harvest meant the village would not worry about food that winter.
sceneCN: 这里说的是「丰产的、物产多的」（第 2 个义项）；句意为丰收让全村那个冬天都不用为吃食发愁。画面里有谷仓、码高的麻袋和堆到门口的谷物。

pos.zh: 充足的；丰富的；丰产的；大量的

derivatives.zh: 由 plentiful 加 -ly 构成，义为「充足地；大量地」
由 plentiful 加 -ness 构成，义为「充足；丰富」
由 plenty 的词干加 -eous 构成，文学用语，义为「丰盛的」
借拉丁 plenitudo 而来，与 plentiful 同源，义为「丰足；充满」

senses.title: More than enough for the need
senses.definition: present in an amount large enough to cover what is needed, usually with something to spare
senses.definitionCN: 数量大到足以满足需要，通常还有富余
senses.example: The clinic has a plentiful supply of clean water.
senses.exampleCN: 诊所的干净用水供应充足。
senses.why: The adjective is plenty plus -ful, so it describes a supply that is literally full rather than merely adequate.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词由名词 plenty 加 -ful 构成，字面就是「满满的」，强调的不是刚好够用，而是有余。

senses.title: Yielding a large amount
senses.definition: producing a large amount of something, said of land, a season, a harvest or a region
senses.definitionCN: 产出很多东西，用来形容土地、季节、收成或地区
senses.example: The valley is famous for its plentiful fruit.
senses.exampleCN: 这道山谷以盛产水果闻名。
senses.why: Land and seasons are judged by what they give, so the same word moves from the size of a supply to the generosity of its source.
senses.whyCN: 土地和季节是按它们给出的东西来评价的，于是这个词从「供给多」滑到「源头慷慨」。

senses.title: Present in large numbers
senses.titleCN: 大量存在的；为数众多的
senses.definition: found in large numbers, as with examples, opportunities or mistakes rather than physical goods
senses.definitionCN: 数量很多地存在，多用于例子、机会、错误等，而非具体货物
senses.example: Plentiful examples make the grammar rule easier to remember.
senses.exampleCN: 大量例子让这条语法规则更容易记住。
senses.why: Once the word means an oversized amount, it can count anything that keeps appearing, not only goods stacked on a shelf.
senses.whyCN: 这个词一旦表示「数量超出所需」，凡是一再出现的东西都能用它来数，不再限于货架上的货品。

intro.en: Plentiful is the adjective built on the noun plenty, and both go back through French to a Latin adjective meaning full.
intro.cn: plentiful 是在名词 plenty 上加后缀构成的形容词，二者都经法语上溯到一个意为「满的」的拉丁形容词。

items.en: Plenus meant full, and it is the root behind both plenty and plentiful.
items.cn: plenus 意为「满的」，是 plenty 与 plentiful 共同的根。

items.en: The noun plenitas named fullness or abundance, the state of being full.
items.cn: 名词 plenitas 指「满、充足」，也就是处于装满的状态。

items.en: Old French plente carried that abundance into French and was used of crops, food and wealth.
items.cn: 古法语 plente 把这层「充足」带入法语，常用于庄稼、食物与财富。

items.en: Middle English took plente as a noun for abundance and later formed an adjective from it.
items.cn: 中古英语把 plente 借作表示「充足」的名词，后来又由它造出形容词。

items.en: Modern English settled the spelling plentiful, using -ful to say that something is full of plenty.
items.cn: 现代英语把拼写固定为 plentiful，用 -ful 表示「充满 plenty」。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the nouns and adjectives of the Latin full family; the near-meaning group gathers adjectives for large amounts.
note.cn: 形近组收拉丁语「满」这一族的名称与形容词；近义组收表示「数量多」的形容词。

entries.definition: The noun behind the adjective, meaning a large amount.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词背后的名词，义为「大量；充足」。

entries.definition: An older adjective for abundant, now mostly literary.
entries.definitionCN: 较老的「丰盛」形容词，现多为文学用语。

entries.definition: The state of being full or complete.
Full or complete, as in a meeting with all members present.
Existing in large quantities, often more formally than plentiful.
entries.definitionCN: 大量存在的，比 plentiful 更正式。

entries.definition: Enough and often more than enough for a purpose.
Produced in large amounts, especially of writing or notes.
entries.definitionCN: 大量产生的，多指文字或笔记。

entries.definition: Generous and giving a lot, often of a harvest.
entries.definitionCN: 慷慨而丰盛的，多形容收成。

normalIntro.en: The adjective is simply the noun plenty wearing the suffix -ful, so every image of a full storehouse belongs to it.
normalIntro.cn: 这个形容词就是名词 plenty 披上 -ful 这件外套，所以凡是「满仓」的画面都归它管。

normal.en: Plentiful is plenty plus -ful, so the ending says full of plenty rather than merely enough.
normal.cn: plentiful 就是 plenty 加 -ful，后缀表明的是「充满大量」，而不只是「够用」。

normal.en: The Latin root plenus, meaning full, also hides inside plenary and plenitude, which both stress completeness.
normal.cn: 拉丁词根 plenus 意为「满」，也藏在 plenary 与 plenitude 里，两者都强调「完备」。

normal.en: Plentiful goes with supplies and harvests, because it measures a stock rather than a single object.
normal.cn: plentiful 常与 supply、harvest 一类词搭配，因为它衡量的是存量，而不是单个物件。

normal.en: The adverb plentifully keeps the same meaning and simply adds the manner of giving.
normal.cn: 副词 plentifully 意思不变，只是补上「以何种方式给予」。

normal.en: Unlike plenty, the adjective cannot stand alone before a noun without naming what is abundant.
normal.cn: 与名词 plenty 不同，这个形容词放在名词前时，必须说清是什么东西充足。

abstract.en: A word built from full describes not just quantity but the relief of not having to count.
abstract.cn: 一个由「满」构成的词，描述的不只是数量，还有不必再数的安心。

abstract.en: Plentiful land is judged by what it gives away, which is why the same word can praise a valley.
abstract.cn: 丰饶的土地是按它给出的东西来评价的，所以同一个词也能用来夸一道山谷。

abstract.en: When examples are plentiful, abundance stops being about food and becomes about chances to learn.
abstract.cn: 当例子变得 plentiful，充足就不再关乎食物，而关乎学习的机会。

examples.en: The clinic has a plentiful supply of clean water.
examples.cn: 诊所的干净用水供应充足。

examples.en: The valley is famous for its plentiful fruit.
examples.cn: 这道山谷以盛产水果闻名。

examples.en: Plentiful examples make the grammar rule easier to remember.
examples.cn: 大量例子让这条语法规则更容易记住。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「扑棱提否」——粮袋扑棱棱堆到提不动，多到让人直说「否」也不必愁，就是 plentiful。

root: 拉丁语 plenus（满的）→ plenitas（充足）→ 古法语 plente → 英语名词 plenty，再加后缀 -ful 构成 plentiful。

sensesIntro.en: The core sense is a stock that is more than full; from it come the producing land, and then any set of repeated instances.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是「装得满满的存量」；由此分出丰产的土地，再扩展到任何一再出现的事物。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: sacks stacked to the roof of a barn, with another one still within reach.
core.cn: 核心意象：麻袋一直码到谷仓屋顶，伸手还够得着下一袋。

branches.en: a water tank filled past the mark
branches.cn: 水罐装到刻度线以上

branches.cn: 果树被果实压弯

intro.cn: 这个形容词由拉丁语的「满」加上英语表示「充满」的后缀构成，所以它把「满」这层意思叠了两遍。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.

definition_zh: 碎片；片段；碎裂
definition_en: a small broken piece, an incomplete part, or to break into pieces
core_image: 一只瓷碗摔在地上，散成许多小片
scene: 地上有一块玻璃碎片。 A fragment of glass lay on the floor.
sceneCN: 这里 fragment 是「碎片」（第 1 个义项）；句意：地上有一块玻璃碎片。

derivatives.zh: 碎裂；分裂
零碎的

senses.title: A broken piece
senses.definition: a small piece broken off something
senses.definitionCN: 从某物上断下的一小块
senses.example: A fragment of glass lay on the floor.
senses.exampleCN: 地上有一块玻璃碎片。
senses.why: This is the basic broken-piece sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是最基本的碎片义项。

senses.title: An incomplete part
senses.definition: a small part of a whole story, song, or text
senses.definitionCN: 故事、歌曲或文章中的一小部分
senses.example: Only a fragment of the letter survived.
senses.exampleCN: 这封信只留下一个片段。
senses.why: A piece of writing can be broken like a thing.
senses.whyCN: 文字也能像物体一样被截断。

senses.title: To break into pieces
senses.definition: to break or separate into small parts
senses.definitionCN: 破碎或分离成小块
senses.example: The old empire fragmented into small states.
senses.exampleCN: 旧帝国分裂成许多小国。
senses.why: The noun became an action.
senses.whyCN: 名词转化成了动作。

intro.en: Fragment comes from the Latin word for a broken piece.
intro.cn: fragment 来自拉丁语中表示碎片的词。

items.en: Frangere meant to break.
items.cn: frangere 意为打破。

items.en: Fragmentum meant a broken piece.
items.cn: fragmentum 意为碎片。

items.en: English borrowed it as fragment.
items.cn: 英语借入时写作 fragment。

items.en: It described pieces of stone and text.
items.cn: 它用来指石头和文字的碎片。

items.en: The verb meant to break apart.
items.cn: 动词形式表示碎裂。

note.en: Fragment is compared with similar-looking words and with piece words.
note.cn: 把 fragment 与形近词以及表示碎片的词作比较。

abstract.en: A fragment remembers the shape of the whole.

abstract.en: Small pieces can still tell a story.
abstract.cn: 小小的碎片仍能讲述故事。

abstract.en: Breaking apart is also a way to begin.
abstract.cn: 破碎也是一种开始。

examples.en: The dish broke into fragments.
examples.cn: 盘子碎成了几片。

dict_mnemonic.text: fragment 与 fraction 同根，都来自「打破」：被打破的一片是碎片，文字少了一截是片段。

root: 源自拉丁语 fragmentum（碎片），来自 frangere（打破），核心义「破碎的一片」。

sensesIntro.en: Fragment means a broken piece, an incomplete part, or to break apart.

branches.en: Glass breaks into sharp pieces.
branches.cn: 玻璃碎成锋利的片。

branches.en: The empire splits into states.

branches.en: Things and texts can both break.
branches.cn: 物体和文字都能破碎。

branches.en: A part is what is left after breaking.

definition_zh: 驴；蠢人；苦差事（donkey work）
definition_en: a small horse-like animal with long ears, a foolish person, or the dull hard work called donkey work
core_image: 山道上一头驮着两袋玉米的小牲口，耳朵又长又直
scene: 山道上，一头灰褐色的小牲口驮着两袋玉米慢慢往前挪。 The donkey stopped beside the well and refused to move.
sceneCN: 这里 donkey 是「驴」（第 1 个义项：一种耳朵很长、常用来驮物的家畜）；句意是那头驴在井边停下，怎么也不肯走。

collocations.zh: 苦差事；单调繁重的工作

derivatives.zh: 由本词加 work 构成的复合词，义为「单调繁重的苦差事」
由本词加 jacket 构成的复合词，义为「工装夹克」
由本词加 years 构成的习语，义为「很长时间」

senses.title: A load-carrying animal
senses.definition: a small animal like a horse, with long ears, often used for carrying loads
senses.definitionCN: 一种像马的小型动物，耳朵很长，常用来驮东西
senses.example: A donkey carried the sacks up the narrow path.
senses.exampleCN: 一头驴驮着口袋走上狭窄的山道。
senses.why: The word named the familiar working animal of farms and hill paths, the one that carries what people cannot.
senses.whyCN: 这个词先指农庄与山道上最常见的工作牲口，也就是替人驮东西的那一只。

senses.title: A foolish or stubborn person
senses.definition: a foolish or stubborn person, used informally and often as an insult
senses.definitionCN: 愚蠢或固执的人，属非正式用法，常带侮辱意味
senses.example: Don't be a donkey and sign without reading it.
senses.exampleCN: 别犯傻看都不看就签字。
senses.why: The animal's reputation for stubbornness turned its name into a mild insult for a person who will not listen.
senses.whyCN: 这种动物以固执出名，名字便成了对不肯听话之人的轻蔑称呼。

senses.title: Dull hard work
senses.definition: used in the phrase donkey work for tiring, repetitive work that others avoid
senses.definitionCN: 用于短语 donkey work，指别人不愿干的累人而重复的工作
senses.example: The interns did the donkey work of sorting old files.
senses.exampleCN: 实习生干了整理旧档案这类苦差事。
senses.why: The animal that carries loads without complaint supplies the image for work that is heavy and repetitive.
senses.whyCN: 那种默默驮重物的牲口，正好为繁重又重复的工作提供了画面。

intro.en: Donkey appeared in English in the eighteenth century and its origin is uncertain, though several explanations exist.
intro.cn: donkey 在十八世纪出现于英语，来源不确定，虽有几种解释但都未定论。

items.en: The older word for the animal was ass, from Latin asinus, and it is unrelated to donkey.
items.cn: 这种动物早先叫 ass，来自拉丁语 asinus，与 donkey 没有词源关系。

items.en: Donkey is first recorded in the eighteenth century; the exact first date is uncertain.
items.cn: donkey 最早在十八世纪有记录，确切首见年代不确定。

items.en: One common suggestion links it to dun, a dull brown colour, plus a suffix; this remains a hypothesis.
items.cn: 一种常见说法把它与 dun（暗淡的褐色）加后缀联系起来，但这仍只是假说。

items.en: Another suggestion derives it from a proper name such as Duncan, but no explanation is proven.
items.cn: 另一种说法认为它来自 Duncan 之类的人名，但没有任何解释得到证实。

items.en: The informal sense of a foolish person and the phrase donkey work both spread in the nineteenth century.
items.cn: 「蠢人」的口语义与 donkey work 这一说法都在十九世纪流行起来。

items.en: The animal name now also supplies compounds such as donkey jacket and donkey's years.
items.cn: 这个动物名今天还提供 donkey jacket 与 donkey's years 等说法。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers compounds built on the animal name; the near-meaning group names other load-bearing beasts.
note.cn: 形近组收的是围绕这个动物名构成的复合说法；近义组收的是其他驮运牲口。

entries.definition: Tiring, repetitive work that few people want to do.
entries.definitionCN: 名词短语，义为「苦差事」，指几乎没人愿意干的累人重复工作。

entries.definition: A short heavy work jacket, originally worn by labourers.
entries.definitionCN: 名词短语，义为「工装夹克」，最初是体力劳动者穿的厚短外套。

entries.definition: A very long time, used in informal British speech.
entries.definitionCN: 习语，义为「很久、多年」，属非正式英式说法。

entries.definition: The older English word for a donkey, also used for a foolish person.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「驴」，也指蠢人；是这种动物的旧称。

entries.definition: The offspring of a donkey and a horse, also used for a stubborn person.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「骡」，也指固执的人；是驴与马的后代。

entries.definition: A small donkey, especially one used in Spanish-speaking regions.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「小毛驴」，多用于西班牙语地区。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the animal's real working life and the phrases English built from its name.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子用这种动物真实的工作生活，以及英语由它名字造出的说法。

normal.en: The older word was ass, so donkey is a newer name for the same beast.
normal.cn: 旧称是 ass，donkey 只是同一头牲口后来的新名字。

normal.en: Donkey work is the heavy, repetitive part nobody wants.
normal.cn: donkey work 就是没人愿意干的繁重重复部分。

normal.en: A donkey jacket is work clothing, not something worn by an animal.
normal.cn: donkey jacket 是工装，不是驴穿的外套。

normal.en: Donkey's years means a long time, not an animal's age.
normal.cn: donkey's years 指很久，不是动物的岁数。

normal.en: Calling a person a donkey is an informal insult about stubbornness.
normal.cn: 把人叫作 donkey，是关于固执的非正式侮辱。

abstract.en: Picture long ears beside a well, refusing to take one more step.
abstract.cn: 想象井边一双长耳朵，怎么也不肯再走一步。

abstract.en: Picture two sacks of corn strapped to a small back on a steep path.
abstract.cn: 想象陡峭山道上，两袋玉米绑在一副小小的背上。

abstract.en: Picture a worker carrying the dull load while others talk.
abstract.cn: 想象别人在说话，一个工人却扛着那份枯燥的重活。

examples.en: The donkey carried water up the hill every morning.
examples.cn: 那头驴每天早上驮水上山。

examples.en: Someone has to do the donkey work before the event.
examples.cn: 活动之前总得有人干那些苦差事。

examples.en: I have not seen that shop for donkey's years.
examples.cn: 我很久没见那家店了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「当骑」——山路上驮着东西、当坐骑的那头牲口，就是 donkey。

root: donkey 于十八世纪出现于英语，来源不确定；较旧的同类词是 ass（拉丁语 asinus）。常见假说把它与表示暗褐色的 dun 加后缀联系起来，也有来自人名的说法，均未获证实。驴的固执形象又派生出「蠢人」义与 donkey work 等说法。

sensesIntro.en: One animal name gives the load carrier, a stubborn person, and the heavy work nobody wants.
sensesIntro.cn: 同一个动物名，既给出驮物的牲口，也给出固执的人，还给出没人愿干的繁重活。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a small long-eared animal carrying sacks up a steep path.
core.cn: 核心意象：一头长耳朵的小牲口，驮着口袋走在陡坡上。

branches.en: THE ANIMAL: the first sense is the working donkey on farm and hill paths.
branches.cn: 动物线：第一个义项是农庄与山道上的役用驴。

branches.en: THE PERSON: the second sense transfers the animal's stubborn image to a person.
branches.cn: 人物线：第二个义项把这种动物的固执形象移到人身上。

branches.en: THE WORK: the third sense turns patient load carrying into a phrase for dull labour.
branches.cn: 工作线：第三个义项把默默驮重变成指枯燥劳动的说法。

branches.en: The beast and the burden explain each other: the animal is named for the work it does.
branches.cn: 牲口与重活互相解释：这种动物正是因它所干的活而被使用。

branches.en: A stubborn person and an unpleasant task share the same stubborn animal image.
branches.cn: 固执的人与难缠的活共享同一幅固执动物的画面。

intro.en: Donkey has no Latin root; English builds its phrases and compounds from the animal name itself.
intro.cn: donkey 没有拉丁词根，英语直接用这个动物名搭出短语与复合词。

latinIntro.en: The Latin word for a donkey was asinus, but it is not a cognate, so no Latin family is listed.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语里驴叫 asinus，但它并非同源词，所以这里不列拉丁词族。

items.example: A donkey stood by the gate.
Dun is one suggested source of the name.
items.exampleCN: dun 是这个名字的一种假想来源。

items.example: The ending has no agreed meaning.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾没有公认含义。

items.example: Two donkeys grazed on the slope.
The donkey work took all afternoon.
items.exampleCN: 这些苦差事干了一下午。

items.example: He wore a dark donkey jacket.
items.exampleCN: 他穿着一件深色工装夹克。

items.example: It has been donkey's years since we met.

definition_zh: 焊接；熔接；使紧密结合；名词：焊接处
definition_en: to join pieces of metal by heating their edges until they melt together, or to unite things closely
core_image: 两块铁被高温烧得发白，熔在一起，冷却后成了一道凸起的接缝
scene: 修船厂的工人戴着面罩，蓝白色的火花沿着钢板接缝一路走过去。 He welded a patch over the hole in the hull.
sceneCN: 这里 weld 是「焊接」（第 1 个义项：把金属边缘加热熔化后接合）；句意为他用焊补片把船壳的洞焊住。烧白后熔在一起的两块铁，就是这个词的样子。

pos.zh: 动词：焊接、熔接；使紧密结合

collocations.zh: 把一个社区紧密联结起来

derivatives.zh: 加后缀 -er 构成，义为「焊工；焊接设备」
加 -ing 构成，义为「焊接」
加后缀 -able 构成，义为「可焊接的」
由过去分词转形容词，义为「焊接的；紧密结合的」

senses.title: To join metal by heat
senses.titleCN: 焊接：用高温把金属接合
senses.definition: to join pieces of metal by heating them until their edges melt and fuse
senses.definitionCN: 把金属件加热到边缘熔化、融合而接起来
senses.example: The two steel plates were welded along the seam.
senses.exampleCN: 两块钢板沿着接缝被焊在一起。
senses.why: The older sense of the word was to boil or to well up; heat joining two things grew from that image.
senses.whyCN: 这个词更早的意思是「沸腾、涌起」；以热把两件东西连成一体由此长成。

senses.title: To close a gap
senses.titleCN: 焊封：把裂缝或孔洞补上
senses.definition: to close a crack, hole or opening by welding material across it
senses.definitionCN: 用焊接材料把裂缝、孔洞或开口封住
senses.example: They welded the crack shut before the tank was filled.
senses.exampleCN: 油箱装油之前，他们先把裂缝焊封了。
senses.why: A hole is a place where two edges should meet; welding makes them meet again.
senses.whyCN: 孔洞本是两条边缘本该相接之处；焊接让它们重新接上。

senses.title: To unite things closely
senses.titleCN: 紧密结合：使事物连成一个整体
senses.definition: to join or unite things so that they act as one
senses.definitionCN: 把事物连成一体，使之作为一个整体运作
senses.example: Shared work welded the two teams into one group.
senses.exampleCN: 共同的工作把两个团队熔成了一个。
senses.why: The physical fusing is applied to people and plans: once welded, the parts no longer come apart easily.
senses.whyCN: 把熔接的物理过程用到人和计划上：一旦焊住，各部分便不易分开。

senses.title: The joint itself
senses.definition: the place or line where two pieces have been welded
senses.definitionCN: 两件东西被焊在一起的部位或线条
senses.example: Inspect the welds along the frame every year.
senses.exampleCN: 每年检查框架上的焊缝。
senses.why: The action freezes into a thing: what was a hot process is now a line you can inspect.
senses.whyCN: 动作凝固成事物：原本炽热的过程，如今成了可以检查的一条线。

senses.title: In technical compound uses
senses.definition: used in technical terms such as spot weld and weld neck flange
senses.definitionCN: 用于点焊、对焊法兰等技术术语
senses.example: A worker made four spot welds to hold the panel.
senses.exampleCN: 工人打了四个点焊把板子固定住。
senses.why: The trade builds its own fixed names, and weld becomes the second half of them.
senses.whyCN: 这一行当自造固定名称，weld 常居其后半。

intro.en: Weld began as a word for boiling and welling up, and only later became the metalworker's term.
intro.cn: weld 最初表示「沸腾、涌出」，后来才成了金属工的术语。

items.en: Wellan meant 'to boil, to well up', and it is the direct ancestor of the modern word.
items.cn: wellan 意为「沸腾、涌出」，是现代词形的直接祖先。

items.en: The past form and the noun were reinforced by Old Norse vella, which also meant to boil.
items.cn: 它的过去式与名词形式受到古诺尔斯语 vella 的加强，后者同样意为「沸腾」。

items.en: In the sixteenth century the verb was applied to metals heated until they joined, and the meaning shifted.
items.cn: 十六世纪，这个动词被用到加热至连接起来的金属上，词义随之转移。

items.en: Industry made it a craft noun: welder, welding, spot weld.
items.cn: 工业使它成了行当日用词：welder、welding、spot weld。

items.en: The figurative sense, to weld people or ideas together, followed from the physical one.
items.cn: 把人和观念「焊」在一起的比喻义，由物理义引申而来。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words easily confused with weld; the near-meaning group gathers ways of joining materials.
note.cn: 形近组收容易与 weld 混淆的词；近义组收各种连接材料的方式。

entries.definition: A person or machine that welds.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「焊工」或「焊接设备」。

entries.definition: The act of holding and using a tool or power; from a different verb.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「挥动、运用」，出自另一个动词 wield。

entries.definition: An old word for a forested area; unrelated in origin.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，古语指林区，与此词来源无关。

entries.definition: To join metal with a filler that melts at low heat; weaker than welding.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「锡焊、软钎焊」，用低熔点填料，强度不如焊接。

entries.definition: To melt together into one; the general term for what welding does.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「熔合」，是表示焊接所做之事的通用词。

entries.definition: To stick things with an adhesive, not by heat.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「用胶粘」，不靠热。

entries.definition: To join firmly, often used of materials and of people.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「粘合、结合」，多用于材料与人。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Old English wellan and the phrases the word actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子使用真实的古英语 wellan，以及这个词实际出现的短语。

normal.en: Weld began as boiling: two edges boil and run into one.
normal.cn: weld 起于沸腾：两条边缘烧到沸腾，于是连成一体。

normal.en: Weld together is the set phrase; the result is a welded joint.
normal.cn: weld together 是固定搭配，结果就是 welded joint「焊接接头」。

normal.en: Spot weld joins small points, not a whole seam.
normal.cn: spot weld 只焊几个点，不是整条缝。

normal.en: A welder wears a mask because the light is fierce.
normal.cn: 焊工戴面罩，因为弧光刺眼。

normal.en: Teams can be welded too: once joined, they act as one.
normal.cn: 团队也能被 weld：一旦接上，就像一个整体运作。

abstract.en: Picture two steel edges turning white, then running together and cooling into one raised seam.
abstract.cn: 想象两条钢边烧得发白，随后融为一体，冷却后留下一道凸起的接缝。

abstract.en: The word is about becoming one piece rather than being held together: that is why it is stronger than glue.
abstract.cn: 这个词说的是变成一整块，而不是被固定在一起：所以它比胶更牢。

abstract.en: Any two things that must never come apart can be described as welded.
abstract.cn: 任何再也不能分开的两样东西，都可以说成 welded。

examples.en: The workers welded the new beam to the old frame.
examples.cn: 工人把新梁焊到旧框架上。

examples.en: Their friendship was welded by a hard winter together.
examples.cn: 一起熬过的那个寒冬把他们的友谊焊得很牢。

examples.en: Check the welds for cracks after the winter.
examples.cn: 冬天过后检查焊缝有没有裂缝。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「威（weld）尔得」——威尔得师傅一烧一按，两块铁就长在一起：焊接

root: 古英语 wellan「沸腾、涌出」，受古诺尔斯语 vella 影响；十六世纪引申为把金属加热熔接；派生词有 welder、welding、weldable。

sensesIntro.en: Five senses of weld start with heat joining two metal edges, then closing a gap, then binding people, then the joint itself, and finally its technical compounds.
sensesIntro.cn: weld 的五个义项从热把两条金属边接起开始，继而封住裂口、把人联结起来，再指焊出的接缝，最后是技术复合用法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two steel edges glowing white, running together, cooling into one raised seam.
core.cn: 核心意象：两条钢边烧得发白，融为一体，冷却成一道凸起的接缝。

branches.en: HEAT LINE: the arc supplies the heat that lets the edges flow.
branches.cn: 热力线：电弧提供让边缘流动的热。

branches.en: GAP LINE: a crack is closed by filling it with molten metal.
branches.cn: 缺口线：用熔融金属把裂缝填上。

branches.en: PEOPLE LINE: the fusing is applied to teams and friendships.
branches.cn: 人物线：这种熔合被用到团队与友情上。

branches.en: SEAM LINE: the raised trace left when it cools.
branches.cn: 接缝线：冷却后留下的凸起痕迹。

branches.en: TRADE LINE: the craft adds names like spot weld.
branches.cn: 行业线：这一行当添出 spot weld 之类的名称。

intro.en: Weld is a native verb; its derivatives use the common English endings.
intro.cn: weld 是本族动词，派生词用常见的英语词尾。

latinIntro.en: No Latin element is involved here; the related native forms are listed instead.
latinIntro.cn: 此处不涉及拉丁语成分，只列出相关的本族词形式。

definition_zh: 装饰性的；装饰用的
definition_en: made to look attractive rather than to be useful
core_image: 一只只能看、不能盛水的花碗
scene: 那只碗画着花，却从不拿来盛饭。 The plate is purely decorative.
sceneCN: 这里 decorative 指「装饰性的」（第 1 个义项：只为好看而设）；句意是这只盘子纯粹是装饰品。

derivatives.zh: 装饰；装饰品
装饰
装饰性地
装饰性
装饰风格

senses.title: Made to be looked at
senses.definition: meant to please the eye rather than to serve a use
senses.definitionCN: 为了取悦眼睛，而不是为了实用
senses.example: The plate is purely decorative.
senses.exampleCN: 这只盘子纯粹是装饰品。
senses.why: Some things exist for the eye alone, and a word is needed to say so.
senses.whyCN: 有些东西只为眼睛存在，这就需要有个词来说明。

senses.title: Adding beauty to something
senses.definition: having the effect of making a place or an object prettier
senses.definitionCN: 起到让地方或物件变好看的效果
senses.example: The columns are decorative, not structural.
senses.exampleCN: 这些柱子只是装饰，并不承重。
senses.why: A part may look like support while doing only the work of beauty.
senses.whyCN: 一个部件看着像在承重，其实只负责好看。

intro.en: Decorative is Latin decorativus, having the power to adorn, from decorare.
intro.cn: decorative 是拉丁语 decorativus，意为「能装点的」，来自 decorare。

items.en: Decorativus meant having the power to adorn.
items.cn: decorativus 指具备装点的能力。

items.en: The -ivus suffix marked a quality rather than an act.
items.cn: -ivus 这个后缀标示的是一种性质，而非动作。

items.en: Décoratif described things that serve beauty.
items.cn: décoratif 形容为美服务的东西。

items.en: Decorative entered English with talk of the fine arts.
items.cn: decorative 随美术的话题进入英语。

items.en: It now separates the beautiful from the useful.
items.cn: 如今它把好看与实用区分开来。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the -ative shape, and the meaning group names beauty with no use.
note.cn: 形近组共享 -ative 的形状，近义组则都在说没有实用、只有好看的属性。

entries.definition: polite and correct in behaviour
copied from something else
likely to mislead
used as decoration
elaborate and not plain
pleasing to look at

normalIntro.en: These hooks begin with a bowl that is never used and end with a pillar that holds nothing up.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从一只从不用来盛东西的碗开始，落到一根什么也不承的柱子。

normal.en: A decorative plate is beautiful and hungry.
normal.cn: 装饰盘很美，而且永远空着。

normal.en: Something decorative earns its place by being seen.
normal.cn: 装饰性的东西靠被看见来证明自己的位置。

normal.en: The prettiest buttons never do up anything.
normal.cn: 最好看的扣子，从来不扣住什么。

normal.en: Beauty that pretends to be structure is the best disguise.
normal.cn: 装成结构的美丽，是最好的伪装。

normal.en: Decorat- is the stem, -ive is the label, useful or not.
normal.cn: decorat- 是词干，-ive 是标签，至于有没有用另说。

abstract.en: Picture a painted bowl on a shelf.
abstract.cn: 想象架子上摆着一只画了花的碗。

abstract.en: Picture a column that ends in mid air.
abstract.cn: 想象一根在半空中就断了的柱子。

abstract.en: Picture a curtain that hides nothing.
abstract.cn: 想象一道什么也没遮住的帘子。

examples.en: The plate is purely decorative.
examples.cn: 这只盘子纯粹是装饰品。

examples.en: Decorative tiles cover the whole wall.
examples.cn: 装饰瓷砖铺满了整面墙。

examples.en: The handle is decorative but still works.
examples.cn: 这个把手是装饰性的，但仍然能用。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 decorative 记成「得客来秀」：de 是得，corative 听着像「客来秀」，客人来了就秀一秀那些只为好看的东西。

root: 来自拉丁语 decorativus（能装点的），后缀 -ivus 表示性质，源头仍是 decorare（装点）与 decus（美与荣誉）。十八世纪随美术话题进入英语，用来区分「只为好看」与「真正有用」。

sensesIntro.en: From an object made only for the eye, to a part that adds beauty without bearing weight.
sensesIntro.cn: 从只为眼睛而做的物件，到只添美而不承重的部件。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a painted bowl that never holds water.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只画着花、从不盛水的碗。

branches.en: The first sense is an object with no job but to be seen.
branches.cn: 第一个义项是除被看见之外没有任务的东西。

branches.en: The second sense is a part that beautifies something else.
branches.cn: 第二个义项是给别的东西添美的部件。

branches.en: Both senses put beauty ahead of function.
branches.cn: 两个义项都把好看放在功用前面。

branches.en: One names a whole object, the other a part of one.
branches.cn: 一个指整个物件，一个指物件的一部分。

branches.en: A decorative part often pretends to be a working one.
branches.cn: 装饰性的部件，常常装成有用的样子。

intro.en: Decorative is the adjective of quality in the decorate family.
intro.cn: decorative 是 decorate 一族里表示性质的那个形容词。

latinIntro.en: The Latin suffix -ivus marks a quality, added to decorare, to adorn.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁后缀 -ivus 表示性质，加在 decorare（装点）之上。

items.example: A decorative arch frames the door.
items.exampleCN: 一道装饰性的拱框住了门。

items.example: They decorate the shop each winter.
items.exampleCN: 他们每年冬天装饰店铺。
装饰工建议用更暖的颜色。
石头被摆成装饰的样子。

items.example: They praised the decorativeness of the gate.
items.exampleCN: 他们称赞这道门的装饰性。
没有装饰的墙显得冷峻。

definition_zh: 跪下；跪着；屈膝
definition_en: to go down or rest on one or both knees, as in prayer, respect, or obedience
core_image: 礼拜堂里一个人双膝落地，脊背挺直，头微微低下
scene: 老教堂的长椅之间，木地板被磨得发亮。 She knelt beside the pew and prayed quietly for a long minute.
sceneCN: 这里 kneel 是「跪下、跪着」（第 1 个义项：用膝盖着地），句意是她在长椅旁跪下，安静地祷告了很长一分钟。画面里有老教堂、长椅与磨亮的木地板。

pos.zh: 动词：跪下；跪着；屈膝（表示敬意或服从）

derivatives.zh: 由动词加 -ing 构成，义为「跪姿、跪着」
加 -er 构成，义为「跪垫、下跪的人」
与 kneel 同源的名词，义为「膝盖」

senses.title: To go down on the knees
senses.definition: to go down onto the knees or rest with the weight on them
senses.definitionCN: 用膝盖着地，或把身体重量压在膝上
senses.example: He knelt down to tie the child shoe.
senses.exampleCN: 他跪下给孩子系鞋带。
senses.why: The verb describes the movement of the body onto its knee, a posture reached from standing.
senses.whyCN: 这个动词描述身体下沉到膝盖上的动作，是一种从站立到达的姿势。

senses.title: To show respect or submission
senses.definition: to kneel as a sign of reverence toward a person, a god, or a power
senses.definitionCN: 为向人、神或权力表示敬意而下跪
senses.example: The knights knelt before the queen.
senses.exampleCN: 骑士们在女王面前跪下。
senses.why: Because lowering the body means lowering oneself, the plain posture became the gesture of respect and surrender.
senses.whyCN: 因为压低身体就意味着压低自己，这一姿势便成为敬意与臣服的姿态。

senses.title: To pray while kneeling
senses.definition: to pray with the body on the knees, as many traditions do
senses.definitionCN: 像许多传统那样，双膝落地地祈祷
senses.example: The whole family knelt together every evening.
senses.exampleCN: 全家人每晚一起跪下祷告。
senses.why: Prayer made the posture a routine, so the verb often implies what is being done in that position.
senses.whyCN: 祷告让这种姿势成了常规，所以这个动词常暗含在这个姿势里所做的事。

intro.en: Kneel is the verb matching the noun knee, and both come from one Old English root.
intro.cn: kneel 是与名词 knee 相配的动词，二者出自同一个古英语词根。

items.en: The verb cneowlian described going down on the knees, beside the noun cneo.
items.cn: 动词 cneowlian 描述跪下的动作，与名词 cneo 并列。

items.en: Northern texts also show cneolian, and both forms share the silent k of the noun family.
items.cn: 北部文本又见 cneolian，两种形式都带着词族中不发音的 k。

items.en: The form settles as knelen, and the past tense knelede later shrinks to knelt.
items.cn: 词形定为 knelen，过去式 knelede 后来缩为 knelt。

items.en: English keeps knelt as the usual past tense, with kneeled as a common American variant.
items.cn: 英语以 knelt 为常用过去式，kneeled 则是常见的美式变体。

items.en: The verb is now used for prayer, respect, obedience, and the practical act of getting low to work.
items.cn: 如今这个动词用于祈祷、致敬、服从，以及低身干活这样的实用动作。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words with the same silent k and the same vowel; the near-meaning group gathers postures and related actions.
note.cn: 形近组收同样带不发音的 k 与同样元音的词；近义组收其他姿势与相关动作。

entries.definition: The noun from the same Old English root, naming the joint that bends.
entries.definitionCN: 同出古英语词根的名词，指那处会弯的关节。

entries.definition: Sounds almost the same but means to press and fold dough.
entries.definitionCN: 读音几乎相同，但意思是按压折叠面团。

entries.definition: Written without the n, and names the spine of a ship.
To bend low with the knees, keeping the feet flat.
To sit with the knees bent and the weight on the feet, without the knees touching the ground.
entries.definitionCN: 屈膝坐着，重量落在脚上，膝盖不触地。

entries.definition: To bend the upper body as a greeting or sign of respect.
entries.definitionCN: 弯下上半身表示问候或敬意。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Old English pair, the two past forms, and the scenes where kneeling happens.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子使用真实的古英语一对词、两种过去式，以及下跪实际发生的场景。

normal.en: Kneel and knee come from the same Old English root; the verb is the noun in motion.
normal.cn: kneel 与 knee 同出古英语词根；动词就是运动中的名词。

normal.en: The k is silent, just as in knee, knife and knock.
normal.cn: k 不发音，和 knee、knife、knock 一样。

normal.en: British English prefers knelt; American English also uses kneeled.
normal.cn: 英式英语偏好 knelt，美式英语也用 kneeled。

normal.en: Kneel down adds nothing in meaning but adds the direction of the movement.
normal.cn: kneel down 没有增加意义，只补出动作的方向。

normal.en: Kneeling in prayer is the most common use of the word.
normal.cn: 祈祷时下跪是这个词最常见的用法。

abstract.en: Going down on the knees is the shortest way to make oneself smaller than the person in front.
abstract.cn: 双膝落地是把自己在对方面前压低的最短路径。

abstract.en: The posture is a sentence without words: the body says what the mouth might not.
abstract.cn: 这个姿势是一句不用词的话：身体说出嘴未必说出的意思。

abstract.en: The same verb covers prayer and tying a shoelace, since the body does not know the difference.
abstract.cn: 同一个动词既指祈祷也指系鞋带，因为身体不做这种区分。

examples.en: She knelt to look the child in the eye.
examples.cn: 她蹲跪下来，与孩子平视。

examples.en: The crowd knelt as the procession passed.
examples.cn: 队伍经过时人群跪下。

examples.en: He was still kneeling in the garden when the rain began.
examples.cn: 雨下起来时他还在花园里跪着。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「尼尔」——膝盖一弯，人就矮了一截

root: 古英语动词 cneowlian / cneolian（跪下），与名词 cneo「膝」同源，共有一个后来不发音的 k；中古英语 knelen，过去式由 knelede 缩为 knelt，美式另作 kneeled。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses: the physical act of going down on the knees, the same act as a sign of respect, and the prayer made in that posture.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项：用膝着地的身体动作，同样动作所表示的敬意，以及在这个姿势里所做的祈祷。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a body lowering until its weight rests on the knees.
core.cn: 核心意象：身体下沉，直到重量落在双膝上。

branches.en: THE BODY: the plain movement from standing to resting on the knees.
branches.cn: 身体线：从站立到以膝支撑的直白动作。

branches.en: THE GESTURE: the low posture becomes a sign of honour or surrender.
branches.cn: 姿态线：低下的姿势成为致敬或臣服的标志。

branches.en: THE PRAYER: in many traditions prayer is made on the knees.
branches.cn: 祈祷线：许多传统中祈祷就是在膝上完成的。

branches.en: THE ROOT LINE: the verb and the noun knee share one Old English origin.
branches.cn: 词根线：这个动词与名词 knee 共有一个古英语来源。

branches.en: THE FORM LINE: knelt and kneeled are both accepted past forms.
branches.cn: 形式线：knelt 与 kneeled 都是可接受的过去式。

intro.en: Kneel is a native verb whose family is small: inflection, a few suffixes, and the noun knee beside it.
intro.cn: kneel 是本土动词，词族很小：词形变化、几个后缀，以及一旁的同源名词 knee。

latinIntro.en: Kneel has no Latin ancestry; the Latin words below refer to the same posture only as comparisons.
latinIntro.cn: kneel 没有拉丁语血统，下面这些拉丁词只是同一姿势的对照。

items.meaning: to go down on the knees

items.example: The man kneeling is a guide.
items.exampleCN: 跪着的那个男人是向导。

items.meaning: one who, or a thing for
items.example: It forms kneeler, a kneeling cushion.
The knee rests on the cushion.

items.exampleCN: 它把 kneel 变成 kneels。

latinEntries.structure: Latin verb from genu and flectere

definition_zh: 侮辱；辱骂；侮辱性的言行
definition_en: to say or do something rude that offends someone, or such an offensive remark
core_image: 一个人当众把对方的东西扔到地上，转头就走
scene: 饭桌上本来还有笑声，一句话出口后所有人都不说话了。 He did not mean to insult her, but the joke was cruel.
sceneCN: 这里 insult 是动词「侮辱」（第 1 个义项：说或做冒犯他人的无礼之事），句意是他并不是想侮辱她，但那个玩笑很伤人。画面里能看到的物件：餐具、被扔下的东西、沉默的餐桌。

pos.zh: 名词：侮辱；侮辱性的言行

derivatives.zh: 由现在分词构成，义为「侮辱性的」
由 insulting 加 -ly 构成，义为「带侮辱地」
由过去分词构成，义为「感到受辱的」

senses.title: To speak or act rudely
senses.definition: to say or do something that shows disrespect and makes someone feel hurt or angry
senses.definitionCN: 说出或做出表示不尊重、使对方受伤或愤怒的言行
senses.example: He insulted the waiter and then left without paying.
senses.exampleCN: 他侮辱了服务员，然后没付钱就走了。
senses.why: Latin insultare means to leap upon; an insult is a verbal leap onto someone else's dignity.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 insultare 意为「跳上去攻击」；侮辱是言语上跳到别人尊严上的攻击。

senses.title: A rude remark or act
senses.definition: a remark or action that is deliberately disrespectful
senses.definitionCN: 故意表示不敬的话语或举动
senses.example: Calling the work amateur was an insult to the whole team.
senses.exampleCN: 说这份工作是业余水平，是对整个团队的侮辱。
senses.why: The verb becomes a countable noun: each leap becomes a named thing you can take.
senses.whyCN: 动词转为可数名词：每一次「扑击」都变成一件可以「承受」的具体事。

senses.title: Something felt as disrespect
senses.definition: an event or offer that seems to show contempt, often unintentionally
senses.definitionCN: 看似表示轻蔑、往往并非有意的事件或提议
senses.example: Offering her the smaller office seemed like an insult.
senses.exampleCN: 给她那间小办公室，看来像是一种侮辱。
senses.why: The sense depends on the receiver: the same act insults one person and not another.
senses.whyCN: 这一义取决于接受方：同一行为对某些人是侮辱，对另一些人不是。

intro.en: Insult comes from Latin insultare "to leap upon", originally used of jumping on an enemy or a fallen body.
intro.cn: insult 来自拉丁语 insultare「跳上去」，最初用于跳上敌人或倒地的身体。

items.en: Salire "to leap" is the root behind assault and result as well as insult.
items.cn: salire「跳」是 assault、result 与 insult 共同的词根。

items.en: Insultare meant to leap upon, and by extension to trample or mock.
items.cn: insultare 意为「跳上去」，引申为践踏、嘲弄。

items.en: The verb was common in the Latin Bible for mocking the fallen.
items.cn: 这一动词在拉丁语圣经中常用于嘲笑倒地之人。

items.en: Old French insulter entered English with the sense of mocking words.
items.cn: 古法语 insulter 带着「言语嘲弄」义进入英语。

items.en: The noun split its pronunciation: stress on the first syllable in modern use.
items.cn: 名词与动词读音分化：现代名词重音在第一音节。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the Latin "leap" root; the near-meaning group holds other words for offensive speech.
note.cn: 形近组共享拉丁「跳」词根；近义组收其他表示冒犯性言语的词。

definition_zh: 脾气；情绪；坏心情；回火；韧性；使缓和；调和
definition_en: a person's state of mind, especially regarding anger; also the hardness of metal, or to soften something
core_image: 一块烧红的铁被浸入冷水，狠劲收成了刚韧
scene: 铁匠把烧红的刀刃浸进水里，狠狠的火气一下子被驯服。 The blacksmith used cold water to temper the hot blade.

senses.title: A state of mind or mood
senses.definition: the particular state of mind someone is in at a moment
senses.definitionCN: 某人一时的情绪状态
senses.example: She is in a cheerful temper today.
senses.exampleCN: 她今天心情很好。
senses.why: The core is a proper mixture: a mood is the current blend inside a person, measured like a mix of ingredients.
senses.whyCN: 核心是「恰当的调配」：心情就是人此刻体内的配比状态，像混合物般可浓可淡。

senses.title: The tendency to become angry
senses.definition: a tendency to become angry easily, especially in lose or keep one's temper
senses.definitionCN: 易怒的倾向，多用于 lose/keep one's temper
senses.example: He lost his temper when the file was deleted.
senses.exampleCN: 文件被删后他发了火。
senses.why: Anger is the mixture boiling over: losing temper means the blend escapes its measure.
senses.whyCN: 愤怒是配比沸腾溢出：lose one's temper 就是情绪冲出了它的「分寸」。

senses.title: The hardness of a metal
senses.definition: the degree of hardness and elasticity given to steel by heating and cooling
senses.definitionCN: 钢经加热冷却后获得的硬度与弹性
senses.example: The blade has a fine temper.
senses.exampleCN: 这把刀刃韧性极佳。
senses.why: Metal treated by fire and water holds the same idea: qualities mixed to the right degree.
senses.whyCN: 金属经水火处理仍循同一理念：把种种性质调配到恰当程度。

senses.title: Make something less severe
senses.definition: to make a feeling or action less strong by mixing in something gentler
senses.definitionCN: 掺入较温和的成分使情感或做法变得不那么激烈
senses.example: His anger was tempered by humour.
senses.exampleCN: 幽默冲淡了他的怒气。
senses.why: To temper literally means to mix in due proportion; softening is adding a mild ingredient to the blend.
senses.whyCN: temper 的字面义是「按比例调和」；缓和就是往混合物里加一味温性的成分。

senses.title: Harden metal by heating and cooling
senses.definition: to heat and cool metal to give it the required hardness
senses.definitionCN: 通过加热与冷却使金属达到所需的硬度
senses.example: The smith tempered the blade in cold water.
senses.exampleCN: 铁匠在冷水中给刀刃回火。
senses.why: The workshop sense is the mixture made physical: fire, water and metal blended into toughness.
senses.whyCN: 工坊义把「调配」落到实物：火、水与金属被调和成刚韧之材。

senses.title: A bad mood, an angry state
senses.definition: an occasion of sudden anger, as in a fit of temper
senses.definitionCN: 一阵突然的怒气，用于 a fit of temper
senses.example: The child threw a fit of temper in the shop.
senses.exampleCN: 孩子在店里大发脾气。
senses.why: When the mixture boils fully, the outburst itself is called a temper: a storm of the blend.
senses.whyCN: 当配比彻底沸腾，爆发的怒气本身也被称作 temper：一场情绪风暴。

intro.en: Temper comes from Latin temperare, to mix in due proportion, the same verb that gives temperature and temperate.
intro.cn: temper 源自拉丁语 temperare「按适当比例调和」，与 temperature、temperate 同源。

items.en: Temperare meant to mix properly, to keep a thing within due measure.
items.cn: temperare 意为妥善调配，使事物保持在适当限度内。

items.en: The deeper origin of temperare is debated; a link with tempus, time or season, is often proposed but not proven.
items.cn: temperare 的更早来源有争议；常被联系到 tempus「时间、时节」，但并未确证。

items.en: The word entered Old English as temprian through church Latin, first of timbers and then of minds.
items.cn: 该词经教会拉丁语进入古英语作 temprian，先指木料调配，后指心性。

items.en: Mood, anger and the blending of qualities all gathered under temper.
items.cn: 中世纪英语中，情绪、怒气与性质调配都汇入 temper。

items.en: Metalworkers gave temper its workshop sense, and psychology kept the mood sense.
items.cn: 近代金工赋予 temper 回火义，而心理层面保留情绪义。

definition_en: a wrong belief or idea that someone holds because a fact, a word or a situation has been understood incorrectly
core_image: 一张画错方向的路线图，被人当成真的，越走越远
scene: 课堂上，一个学生把地图上的南北认反了，照着这张图走了很久，离目的地越来越远。 Many people hold the misconception that we use only a small part of our brains.
sceneCN: 这里是「错误观念」（第 1 个义项：被当成真的错误想法）；句意为很多人误以为我们只用了大脑的一小部分。图中可辨识物件：认反的地图、走远的身影、远处的目的地。

senses.title: A mistaken belief held as true
senses.definition: a wrong belief that a person accepts as true because something has been understood incorrectly
senses.definitionCN: 因为把某件事理解错了，而把错误的想法当成真的
senses.example: It is a misconception that goldfish remember nothing.
senses.exampleCN: 认为金鱼什么都记不住，是一种误解。
senses.why: Conception names the mind's act of forming an idea, and mis- marks that act as a wrong turn, so the word points at an idea built on a faulty grasp rather than at a single mistaken fact.
senses.whyCN: conception 指头脑中形成想法的动作，mis- 把这个动作标成走偏的一步，所以这个词指向建立在错误理解上的想法，而不只是一条记错的事实。

senses.title: A false idea shared by many people
senses.definition: an inaccurate idea that circulates widely among people and is repeated without being checked
senses.definitionCN: 在人群中广泛流传、被反复转述却无人核对的错误看法
senses.example: The belief that sugar makes children hyperactive is a widespread misconception.
senses.exampleCN: 认为糖会让孩子过度活跃，是一种普遍的错误看法。
senses.why: An idea spreads when many minds conceive it in the same way, so a private mistake turns into a public one; the word then names the shared version rather than one person's confusion.
senses.whyCN: 当许多头脑以同样的方式形成同一个想法，这个想法就会传开，个人的错误便变成公共的错误；于是这个词指大家共同持有的那个版本，而不是某一个人的糊涂。

senses.title: A wrong reading of a rule, word or text
senses.definition: a mistaken understanding of what a rule, a word or a piece of writing actually requires or says
senses.definitionCN: 对规则、词语或文字实际要求或所说内容产生的错误理解
senses.example: His misconception of the contract led him to sign away the rights.
senses.exampleCN: 他对合同的误解使他签字放弃了权利。
senses.why: If conception is the mind taking hold of a thing, it can take hold of a sentence as well as of the world, so misconceiving a clause produces the same kind of wrong possession.
senses.whyCN: 如果 conception 是头脑抓住一件事，那么它既能抓住世界，也能抓住一句话；把一条款理解错，就等于以同样的方式抓错了东西。

intro.en: Misconception joins an Old English prefix meaning wrong with a Latin noun for the act of forming an idea in the mind.
intro.cn: misconception 由一个表示「错误」的古英语前缀与一个表示「在心中形成想法」的拉丁名词组合而成。

items.en: The prefix mis- already meant wrong, badly or amiss in Old English, and it was added freely to verbs and nouns.
items.cn: 古英语中的前缀 mis- 已表示错误、不当、出了偏差，可以自由地加在动词和名词前面。

items.en: Concipere joined com-, meaning together, to capere, to take, and meant to take hold of something in the mind.
items.cn: concipere 由表示「共同」的 com- 与表示「拿取」的 capere 组合而成，意为在头脑中把握住某物。

items.en: Conceptio named the act of conceiving and also the thing conceived, and English borrowed it as conception.
items.cn: conceptio 既指构想这个动作，也指被构想出来的东西，英语借入后写作 conception。

items.en: English conception covers both the forming of an idea and the beginning of a pregnancy, because both are a taking hold of something new.
items.cn: 英语的 conception 既指形成想法，也指怀孕的开始，因为两者都是把某种新东西接住、握住。

items.en: Modern English put mis- in front of conception, so the word names an idea taken hold of in the wrong way.
items.cn: 现代英语把 mis- 放在 conception 前面，于是这个词指以错误方式把握住的想法。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words built with mis- or on Latin conception; the near-meaning group gathers words for wrong understanding and for ideas that are not true.
note.cn: 形近组收带 mis- 的词以及建立在拉丁语 conception 上的词；近义组收表示错误理解以及不真实想法的词。

entries.definition: To understand something wrongly; built with mis- and conceive.
entries.definitionCN: 把某事理解错；由 mis- 与 conceive 构成。

entries.definition: The forming of an idea in the mind, or the beginning of a pregnancy.
entries.definitionCN: 在头脑中形成想法，或怀孕的开始。

entries.definition: A wrong way of seeing or understanding something, built with mis- and perception.
entries.definitionCN: 对某事的错误看法或理解，由 mis- 与 perception 构成。

entries.definition: A mistaken understanding of a situation or of what someone means.
entries.definitionCN: 对某种情况或他人意思的错误理解。

entries.definition: A failure to understand something correctly, or a small disagreement caused by this.
entries.definitionCN: 没能正确理解某事，或由此引起的小争执。

entries.definition: A false belief, or a piece of reasoning that does not hold.
entries.definitionCN: 错误的想法，或站不住脚的推理。

entries.definition: A false idea or impression, often one that the mind finds pleasant.
entries.definitionCN: 错误的想法或印象，常指让头脑觉得愉快的那种。

entries.definition: A widely repeated story or belief that is not true.
entries.definitionCN: 广为流传却不真实的故事或看法。

normalIntro.en: The word is built from a Germanic prefix for wrongness and a Latin noun for conceiving; its family keeps returning to ideas formed, held and passed on in the wrong shape.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词由表示「错误」的日耳曼语前缀和表示「构想」的拉丁名词构成，同族词反复回到被错误地形成、持有并传播的想法。

normal.en: Mis- means wrong and conception means the forming of an idea, so a misconception is an idea formed the wrong way.
normal.cn: mis- 表示错误，conception 表示形成想法，所以 misconception 就是以错误方式形成的想法。

normal.en: Conception comes from Latin capere, to take; a misconception is an idea taken hold of before anyone checks it.
normal.cn: conception 来自拉丁语 capere（拿取）；misconception 就是还没核对就被抓住的想法。

normal.en: Misconceive is the verb, and misconception is the noun that names the result of conceiving wrongly.
normal.cn: misconceive 是动词，misconception 是名词，指错误构想之后留下的结果。

normal.en: Misperception repeats the same pattern with perception instead of conception, and both describe a wrong grasp of something.
normal.cn: misperception 用 perception 替换 conception，重复了同样的构词方式，两个词都指对某物的错误把握。

normal.en: The word is used of ideas rather than of the senses: we say a misconception about a subject, not a misconception of a sound.
normal.cn: 这个词用于想法而不是感官：我们说对某个主题的误解，而不说对一种声音的误解。

abstract.en: A wrong map carried confidently is the whole picture of a misconception: the traveller is lost in the drawing, not in the land.
abstract.cn: 一张被自信地带着的错误地图就是 misconception 的全部画面：旅人不是迷失在土地上，而是迷失在图纸里。

abstract.en: An error becomes a misconception when it is held as true, which is why the word sounds more settled than a simple mistake.
abstract.cn: 错误一旦被当成真的持有，就成了 misconception，所以这个词听起来比单纯的差错更稳固。

abstract.en: Because the word names the mind's wrong taking hold, correcting one is less about adding facts than about loosening a grip.
abstract.cn: 因为这个词指头脑抓错了东西，纠正它不是往头脑里添事实，而更像是把抓得太紧的手松开。

examples.en: It is a misconception that goldfish remember nothing.
examples.cn: 认为金鱼什么都记不住，是一种误解。

examples.en: The belief that sugar makes children hyperactive is a widespread misconception.
examples.cn: 认为糖会让孩子过度活跃，是一种普遍的错误看法。

examples.en: His misconception of the contract led him to sign away the rights.
examples.cn: 他对合同的误解使他签字放弃了权利。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「米斯康塞普」——米斯把一捆想法接错了线头，整捆都亮成了错的；记住 misconception 是错误观念。

root: 古英语前缀 mis-（错误、不当）加拉丁语 concipere（com- 共同 + capere 抓取，意为「在心中把握」）构成 conceptio（构想），再进入英语为 conception；misconception 即「把握错了的构想」。

sensesIntro.en: The core is an idea formed in the wrong way; the senses divide into a private mistaken belief, a widely shared false idea, and a wrong reading of a text or rule.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是以错误方式形成的想法；义项分为个人持有的错误信念、众人共享的错误看法，以及对文字或规则的错误理解。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a wrongly drawn map carried as if it were true, the walker moving further from the destination.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张画错方向的路线图被人当成真的，走的人离目的地越来越远。

branches.en: a traveller trusting a map whose north is reversed
branches.cn: 旅人相信一张南北颠倒的地图

branches.en: the same wrong claim repeated in a crowded room
branches.cn: 同一句错话在拥挤的房间里被反复转述

branches.en: a signature given to a clause that was read wrongly
branches.cn: 在一句被读错的条款下签了名

branches.en: a saying passed down because nobody stopped to check it
branches.cn: 因为没人停下来核对而流传下来的一句话

branches.en: a corrected page and a hand loosening its grip
branches.cn: 被改正的一页与松开的手

intro.en: The word is carried by a Germanic prefix of wrongness, the Latin verb for taking hold in the mind, its noun and the English noun and verb built on them.
intro.cn: 这个词由表示错误的日耳曼语前缀、拉丁语中「在头脑中把握」的动词及其名词，以及由它们构成的英语名词和动词共同支撑。

latinIntro.en: The first element of the word is Germanic, but its second element comes from Latin, so the Latin side records the conceiving family rather than the prefix.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词的第一个成分来自日耳曼语，第二个成分来自拉丁语，因此拉丁同源部分记录的是「构想」这一词族，而不是前缀。
